thread:
maria: Hey team — quick proposal for a dynamic reshuffle protocol for spot GPU interruptions. TL;DR: try local reshuffle -> soft-drain -> fallback to reserved pool -> escalation if <capacity for 5m.

kevin: +1. Can you outline steps? We need clear k8s commands and automation hooks.

maria: Outline below. Keep it short.
1) Detect interruption window via cloud metadata and spot-notice stream.
2) Snap worker state (checkpoint) if job supports. Prefer incremental ckpt.
3) Soft-drain: cordon + annotate -> signal job gracefully.
4) Live-reshuffle service tries to migrate low-memory jobs to ephemeral CPU nodes.
5) If remaining load > threshold -> route to dedicated pool or throttle new jobs.
6) If unavailable for >5m -> page oncall (sev2) and initiate capacity purchase.

jia: Important: ML training checkpoints vary. Add a per-job grace annotation: infra/ckpt-level=full|incremental|none

samir: We should minimize blocked capacity during drain. Proposal: set pod disruption budgets to 1 per node and prefer preemptible-friendly sched class.

ops-bot: Detected spot instance interruption in us-west1-b for pool gpu-spot-rt. Instance metadata: preemptible=true, shutdown_time=2025-07-12T02:10:12Z

maria: Example commands for soft-drain:

```bash
# cordon node
kubectl cordon gpu-node-124
# annotate to signal job controller
kubectl annotate node/gpu-node-124 infra/reshuffle=soft-drain
# trigger graceful termination hook (custom)
kubectl exec -n infra job-relocator -- /bin/sh -c "relocate --node gpu-node-124"
```

kevin: And fallback routing config snippet (env var for proxy routing):

```yaml
ROUTE_PRIORITY: "spot->reserved->dedicated"
MAX_DIVERT_PERCENT: "40"
THRESHOLD_FREE_GPU: "2"
```

maria: Monitoring/alerts:
- Alert if spot eviction rate > 5% in 10m
- Alert if number of nodes cordoned > 10% cluster
- Alert if fallback to dedicated triggers > 3 times/hour -> cost alert

jia: Test plan: simulate spot notice via metadata server, assert ckpt created, node annotated, pods rescheduled within 90s for short jobs.

samir: Escalation matrix (condensed):
- automated remediation succeeds -> no page
- if fail and capacity deficit > 3 GPUs for >5m -> page infra-oncall (sev2)
- if >30m and customer-facing latency affects API -> page eng-sre (sev1)

maria: Cost guardrails: auto-bid cap per region and max_on_demand_fallback_pct=15 to avoid unbounded spend. We should auto-disable new spot-only workflows during market stress.

kevin: Ops action checklist for oncall:
- run `./scripts/reshuffle-audit --since 10m`
- if shortage persists, run `terraform apply -var 'buy_capacity=true'` in infra/prod

maria: Notes about mixed pools:
- prefer heterogeneous pools (A100+T4) with label-based scheduling
- use eviction-priority labels so high-priority jobs land on reserved
- track per-pool cost-per-effective-token for inference workloads

ops-bot: Reminder: runbook doc updated: https://internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/reshuffle-protocol (edited)

jia: One more — add a perf regression check: if fallback causes median latency >2x baseline, auto-scale dedicated and notify product.

maria: I'll draft the formal runbook page from this thread. If anyone wants to add short commands or edge cases, reply here. :v:

kevin: LGTM. I'll add the terraform snippets and a quick test harness.

samir: Will add PDB and scheduler-name changes to the k8s manifests.
